newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela budget gets first Senate OK, 2nd vote Fri.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela budget gets first Senate OK, 2nd vote Fri.

text.p: Venezuela's Senate approved the government's 7.8 trillion bolivar ($16.6 billion) 1997 budget proposal Thursday and said it would give the bill a second and final reading on Friday.
As in the lower house, the bill was approved with the votes of opposition union-based Radical Cause, social Christian Copei and government-backing Movement to Socialism (MAS) parties.
Leading opposition party social democratic Democratic Action (AD) abstained in disagreement over spending reallocations made to the original budget proposal.
The left-leaning government Convergence party also abstained from several clauses of the bill in disagreement over the spending reallocations made by the other three parties.

According to Central Budget Office (OCEPRE) figures, the 1997 budget is based on a projected inflation rate of 25 percent, an average exchange rate of 490 bolivars per dollar and a growth rate of four percent of GDP.
The Senate also approved the Umbrella Law, which accompanies each budget and specifies how much fresh debt the government can take on each year.
The 1997 Umbrella Law limits the government to up to 159.7 billion bolivars worth of new internal debt and $1.982 billion in foreign debt.
